market_view: VIX jumped 12% on 07-17 to 18.8 (+25% over 5 days) with the semiconductor ETF down 8.9% over 5 days and WTI up 15.5%; a mild risk-off tilt, not a stress regime. Headlines are mostly opinion and press releases.

oil_gas.reasoning: WTI +4.5% on 07-17 and +15.5% over 5 days is already priced in; no XOM, OPEC+ or supply headline in the record. Only a consumer-sentiment item mentions easing gas prices and reduced Middle East tensions. No named catalyst.

gold_miners.reasoning: Gold is 24% below its high and NEM is down 15% over 20 days, but oversold is not a catalyst. No NEM, Fed or dollar headline. The only related items are irrelevant company notices.

chips.reasoning: The semiconductor ETF fell 8.9% over 5 days. Headlines are Motley Fool opinion pieces (Meta in-house chips, memory ETF, Sandisk drop on a Chinese AI model), with no NVDA-specific fact. Earnings season adds variance only.

pharma.reasoning: No LLY headline; the pharma items are small-cap releases (Can-Fite, OKYO, Harrow). LLY is up 30% over 60 days, so a long would rest on momentum, which is not a reason.

copper_uranium.reasoning: FCX fell 15% over 20 days with copper -1.2% on 07-17, but there is no supply, China demand or FCX headline in the record. A pullback alone is not a catalyst.

would_change_my_mind: A named company or commodity headline: an XOM or OPEC+ supply item, an NVDA export-rule or guidance change, an LLY trial or approval result, an FCX or copper supply outage, or a Fed or dollar shift for gold.

handoff.what_changed: Five days since the last note (07-15). WTI rose another 15.5% over 5 days (4.5% on 07-17) to 82.5, while the semiconductor ETF fell 8.9% over 5 days and VIX jumped 12% on 07-17 to 18.8. Headlines again held no leader-specific catalyst.

oil_gas.why: WTI rally already priced in; no XOM or OPEC+ headline.

gold_miners.why: Gold and NEM weak but no NEM, Fed or dollar catalyst.

chips.why: Sector sell-off has only opinion headlines, no NVDA-specific catalyst.

pharma.why: No LLY news; only small-cap pharma releases.

copper_uranium.why: FCX pullback has no supply or demand headline.
